USAFE 2    TT 1524          SECRET          4 Nov 48

To Gen Cabell

     We now have one complete set of all reports prepared by special
intelligence organization of the European Command from its conception to
present date.  We are forwarding these reports for your inspection and
final disposition.  We are of the opinion that inspection of these reports
will lend weight to arguments for allocating Air Force funds to this
organization.  Advise caution in utilizing these reports as most of them
were forwarded as received.

(END OF ITEM)

USAFE 10    TT 1524    CONFIDENTIAL    4 Nov 1948
From OI OB

     Following report on unidentified aircraft sighting comes from 307th Bomb
Group which participated in operation daggar.  Unidentified aircraft was
sighted by three crews of the group at 1402Z 5 Sep 48 off west coast of Holland,
5155N/0355E.  Altitude of all aircraft was 30,000 feet.  When first sighted
the unidentified A/C was cruising at a normal jet speed, heading 120 degrees.
Soon after first seen, A/C began leaving smoke trails and condensation trails
accompanied by sudden acceleration and then climb.  Generall agreed by
observers that it was a single jet propelled A/C employing probably rocket
assists with tremendous reserve power, more than normal curising speed for
jets of the 1947 variety.  Never within identification range; its course
did not indicate its purpose.
Our evaluation of the above:  B-2.
(END OF ITEM)

        USAFE 14          TT 1524     TOP SECRET        4 Nov 1948


From OI OB

        For some time we have been concerned by the recurring reports on flying
saucers.  They periodically continue to cop up; during the last week, one was
observed hovering over Neubiberg Air Base for about thirty minutes.  They
have been reported by so many sources and from such a variety of places that
we are convinced that they cannot be disregarded and must be explained on some
basis which is perhaps slightly beyond the scope of our present intelligence
thinking.

        When officers of this Directorate recently visited the Swedish Air
Intelligence Service.  This question was put to the Swedes.  Their answer
was that some reliable and fully technically qualified people have reached
the conclusion that "these phenomena are obviously the result of a high
technical skill which cannot be credited to any presently known culture on
earth."  They are therefore assuming that these objects originate from some
previously unknown or unidentified technology, possibly outside the earth.

        One of these objects was observed by a Swedish technical expert near
his home on the edge of a lake.  The object crashed or landed in the lake
and he carefully noted its azimuth from his point of observation.  Swedish
intelligence was sufficiently confident in his observation that a naval
salvage team was sent to the lake.  Operations were underway during the
visit of USAFE officers.  Divers had discovered a previously uncharted
crater on the floor of the lake.  No further information is available, but
we have been promised knowledge of the results.  In their opinion, the
observation was reliable, and they believe that the depression on the floor
of the lake, which did not appear on current hydrographic charts, was in
fact caused by a flying saucer.

        Although accepting this theory of the origin of these objects poses a
whole new group of questions and puts much of our thinking in a changed
light, we are inclined not to discredit entirely this somewhat spectacular
theory, meantime keeping an open mind on the subject.  What are your
reactions?

TOP SECRET

(END OF USAFE ITEM 14)







TOP SECRET

TOP SECRET

He also knows of a Soviet-built radar set located near Kholomia Airfield
(5 KM W of Airfield, near the town of Kholomia). This type set is
called "Redut". He believes personnel of this set to be army, assigned
to PVO, but is not certain. His regiment conducted flying cooperation
exercises with the set, presumably to train the set operators, since
the set was first located at Kholomia in Spring 1947. His aircraft, in
October 1948, lost the set on such an exercise at a distance of 150 kilometers
and altitude of 1200 meters. Following instructions, he then climbed to
3000 meters, when the set again picked him up. he states he believes this
type set is standard throughout the PVO, and that he believes its maximum
range to be 150 kilometers, because no training flights of greater distances
were ever undertaken. Further details will be sought.

     All TU-2 of 63 Regt are fitted with IFF type S. CH. (C-4), located
in the tail of the aircraft and operated by a switch in the radio operator's
compartment. Further, experiments with airborne radar (a tail warning
device) werecarried out in 1947 and TU-2 of his regiment. This equipment
involved the installation of a small external array. Sets were removed after
a few days of testing, but results were understood to have been satisfactory.

     On the subject of Kholomia Airfield, this field is currently apparently
simply a level pasture, 600 meters N/S by 1400 meters E/W, but a paved runway
is being constructed outside the north boundary of the airfield. No details
are known to subject, as work has just commenced. The airfield currently has
no installations; aircraft are parked in the open, and fuel is brought
directly to the aircraft from the town of Kholomia (7 kilometers to the N) by
tank trucks.

     Another interesting fact is the arrival of the TU-2 with only a crew
of three, and without the dorsal turret machine gun in place (nor anyplace
on the aircraft). Subject states that the air gunner sergeants who should
occupy this fourth position are on duty with the regiment, but are engaged
in fatigue details, and XXXX rarely carried on training flights.

     Subject believes the TU-2 to be manufactured in a factory in Moscow,
and it is noted that a plaque in the aircraft stated that it had been produced
in Factory No. 19.

     A fuller report will shortly be underway, based on interrogation
conducted so far, and many more details are expected to be obtained in the
next week or two, with both pilot and navigator being interrogated.

(END USFA-1)

summaryJa: 1948年11月のAFO/USAFEの抜粋報告（TT #1524）を収めた文書。主要項目は次の通り。1) USAFE 2（機密）: 欧州軍特殊諜報組織が作成した報告書一式を整備し、資金配分の参考としてジェネラル・キャベルへ回付する旨。報告書は受領時のまま転送されたものが多く、注意を促している。2) USAFE 10（機密扱い）: 1948年9月5日1402Z、307th爆撃群の3機乗員がオランダ西岸付近（51°55'N/03°55'E、3万フィート）で未確認機を目撃。通常のジェット巡航速度から煙・凝結跡を伴い急加速・上昇し、ロケット補助を用いたように見えた。評価はB-2。3) USAFE 14（極秘）: 飛行円盤報告の再発。ノイビーベルク基地上空でのホバリング事例や、スウェーデンの技術者による湖での着水／墜落観測と、潜水隊が発見した未記載の湖底陥没を記述。スウェーデン当局は既知の地上文化によらない高い技術の可能性を示唆しており、USAFEは結論を保留して意見を求めている。4) ソ連関連（極秘）: コロミア（Kholomia）空域付近の“Redut”レーダー、射程約150kmの運用報告、TU-2所属部隊の装備（尾部IFF S.CH.(C-4)、1947年の機上レーダー実験等）、格納や滑走路整備状況、3名乗員で来着したTU-2に背部旋回銃塔が欠如していた旨、製造は工場第19号の銘板あり。追加尋問に基づく詳細報告が予定されている。5) USAFE 16（機密）: CIC情報で、ソ連が在外CSR任務に対しコストを問わず大量のレーダー管と完全なレーダー装置の購入を指示したとの報告（評価C-3）。
summaryEn: Extracts from TT #1524 (USAFE, 4 Nov 1948) containing several intelligence items. Key points: 1) USAFE 2 (Secret): A complete set of reports from the European Command special intelligence organization has been assembled and forwarded to Gen. Cabell for inspection and disposition; caution advised as many reports were forwarded as received. 2) USAFE 10 (Confidential): At 1402Z on 5 Sep 1948, three crews of the 307th Bomb Group observed an unidentified aircraft off the west coast of Holland (51°55'N/03°55'E) at 30,000 ft; the object left smoke/condensation trails, showed sudden acceleration and climb, appeared jet-propelled with probable rocket assist; assessed B-2. 3) USAFE 14 (Top Secret): Recurring flying-saucer reports, including a ~30-minute hover over Neubiberg Air Base and a Swedish technical expert’s observation of an object that crashed/landed in a lake; Swedish salvage/divers found an uncharted depression on the lake floor and consider the observation reliable, suggesting a possibly non‑earth technology; USAFE keeps an open mind and requests reactions. 4) Soviet-related technical/airfield report (Top Secret): Presence of a Soviet 'Redut' radar near Kholomia airfield (approx. 5 km W), believed PVO-operated with ~150 km range; TU-2s of the 63rd Regiment fitted with IFF type S.CH.(C-4); 1947 airborne radar tail-warning tests conducted; Kholomia airfield described as open pasture with runway construction begun; TU-2s arriving with three-man crews and missing dorsal turret; aircraft plaque indicates Factory No. 19; further interrogation reports forthcoming. 5) USAFE 16 (Secret): CIC source reports the Russians have ordered CSR missions abroad to purchase large quantities of radar tubes and a complete radar set regardless of cost (Eval C-3).
